headline: High: firecrawl’s broad network/API access can leak or misapply ComfyUI-generated content, while shared MCP/API pathways create moderate injection and conflict risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can expose outputs through files and a Comfy API, while firecrawl supports MCP-compatible client use and API-driven scraping. That creates a plausible bridge where content from ComfyUI could be fed into firecrawl workflows and treated as instructions or markup. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are copied into firecrawl prompts, scrape inputs, or MCP messages without provenance checks, injection risk exists.
IF firecrawl parses ComfyUI-generated text or metadata as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every handoff between agents.
Strip instructions from generated text before passing it to firecrawl.
Use a fixed schema for inter-agent messages.
Disable any automatic ingestion of ComfyUI outputs into firecrawl.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing at the orchestrator layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, workflows, seeds, and model assets, while firecrawl touches web content, structured data, screenshots, and API keys and has broad network egress. If ComfyUI outputs or local assets are routed into firecrawl, sensitive prompts, seeds, or model artifacts can leave the local environment. The pairwise path is plausible from the profiles alone, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF ComfyUI workflows, seeds, or model artifacts are sent to firecrawl inputs, those data classes can be exposed externally.
IF firecrawl is used on pages containing secrets or API keys, its broad egress can transmit them off-host.
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI and firecrawl on separate workspaces.
Do not pass seeds, checkpoints, or prompts into firecrawl.
Redact API keys before any scrape or crawl.
Review outbound requests for sensitive payloads.
requires-engineering: enforce egress filtering and secret scanning at the integration boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI is offline-first and does not write the filesystem or modify git, but firecrawl supports API/CLI use, MCP-compatible client support, and multiple instances. If both are orchestrated over the same mutable workspace or shared API credentials, their overlapping access can conflict on shared resources even without direct filesystem writes. The profiles do not prove locking, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace or shared credential store, concurrent updates can collide.
IF firecrawl instances run in parallel against the same target resource, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Use distinct API keys per agent.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator queue.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same target resource.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI produces generated artifacts and workflows, while firecrawl is a crawler/extractor that can consume and transform external content. If firecrawl treats ComfyUI output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated metadata can cascade into downstream scraping, indexing, or actions. The profiles show a plausible producer-consumer chain, but not a verified verification step, so medium fits.
conditions: IF firecrawl consumes ComfyUI output without validation, incorrect prompts or metadata can propagate.
IF downstream automation acts on firecrawl results, a bad upstream artifact can trigger incorrect actions.
mitigations: Require schema validation on all ComfyUI outputs.
Insert a human review step before firecrawl acts on generated content.
Compare extracted fields against source URLs.
Log and diff intermediate artifacts.
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and rejection rules for untrusted upstream content.

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI touches local media, workflows, seeds, and model assets, while firecrawl touches web content, screenshots, and API keys and explicitly requests a FIRECRAWL_API_KEY. If regulated or personal data is scraped and then processed by firecrawl, retention and residency obligations may differ from ComfyUI’s local/offline posture. The profiles do not specify certifications, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is scraped by firecrawl and then stored alongside ComfyUI artifacts, retention rules may diverge.
IF the deployment requires residency or deletion guarantees, the profiles do not show matching controls.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Keep regulated data out of firecrawl jobs.
Document retention for both systems.
Separate logs by data class.
requires-engineering: implement residency and deletion controls in the pipeline.
